In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the signal sequence is removed after the preprotein is threaded across the membrane and before the nascent chain emerges into the periplasm.

the signal peptidases in E. coli are not part of the translocon and are located on the inner membrane, but they can be recruited to the exoplasmic surface of the membrane by the translocon to process signal peptides.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
signal peptide processing is an event that occurs after almost complete translocation of the precursor protein across the cytoplasmic membranes in E. coli.

the translocation machinery is capable of maintaining the translocating pre-protein in an unfolded conformation for a long time and that signal peptidases are able to act on the unfolded polypeptide chain even after the translocon is fully assembled.
signal peptidases are the last enzymes to be engaged in the process of translocation of the nascent polypeptide across bacterial membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a signal peptide can be processed by the translocon even after the preprotein has already traversed the membrane and is in the cytoplasm.
the temporal order of events of signal sequence processing and translocation of the bulk of the polypeptides across the membrane is not necessarily fixed.
the signal peptidases in E. coli can act as a gatekeeper to control the rate of pre-protein translocational process.
